I am 54 years old and have farmed my land in Quzhou County since I was a young man. My father taught me how to read the soil and the weather, and I never went beyond primary school because the fields needed hands. I have five mu of flat, good-quality alluvial land near Dongfu village. I do not experiment with strange crops — the grain buyers come to the village every autumn, and they want wheat and maize. That is what I know, and that is what pays.

This year, I will stick to the **winter wheat – summer maize rotation** on all five mu. I cannot afford to leave land fallow or gamble on cotton or vegetables — the water and fertilizer costs are too high, and the market prices fluctuate too much. Wheat and maize have stable demand and government minimum purchase prices.

For **winter wheat**, I will sow an improved variety, *Liangxing 77*, around October 7th, right after I rotary-till the maize stubble into the soil. I will broadcast about 30 jin of seed per mu. For fertilizer, I will put down one bag — about 50 kg — of compound fertilizer (18-22-5) as basal, and top-dress with urea at the jointing stage in spring. The wheat will need three irrigations: one before winter to help it survive the cold, one at jointing, and one during grain filling. I will spray herbicide once in early spring and insecticide once at heading. If I manage it well, I should get about 960 jin per mu.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant **summer maize**, variety *Nongda 372*, a hybrid. I will not till the soil — I will plant directly into the wheat stubble to save time and fuel, because the maize growing season is short and every day counts before autumn frost. I will apply one bag of compound fertilizer (28-6-6) at planting and side-dress urea when the plants reach knee-height. Two irrigations should be enough if the summer rains are normal: one at the big-flare stage and one at filling. I will spray herbicide after emergence and insecticide once during silking to control armyworms. I expect about 1,200 jin per mu.

Irrigation water from the well gets more expensive every year, so I do not water more than necessary. I also do not apply more fertilizer than what the seed dealer and the village extension technician recommend — I have seen neighbors waste money on extra urea that just runs off or burns the plants.

decision.reasoning_summary: I am a 54-year-old smallholder with primary education and five mu of land in Quzhou County. I follow the traditional winter wheat–summer maize double-cropping system because it is the proven, low-risk system for the North China Plain, with reliable buyers and government price support. I use an improved wheat variety and a hybrid maize variety, apply compound fertilizer plus urea topdressing, irrigate three times for wheat and twice for maize, and minimize tillage costs by using no-tillage for maize after wheat harvest. I keep input costs controlled because groundwater irrigation and fertilizers have become expensive, and I have learned from experience that extra inputs beyond the extension recommendation do not pay off.
